title: Twenty dots beat "twenty percent"
question: Twenty dots beat "twenty percent"
hook: Physicians given "90% sensitivity, 9.9% false-positive rate" reason wrongly about a positive test; given the same facts as counts of people, they get it right.
core_idea: Natural frequencies (Gigerenzer) — and their visual form, the quantile dotplot — replace percentage arithmetic with countable individuals, moving the encoding to position and count, the channels people actually decode.
visual_object: a grid of person-dots that regroups from "1,000 women" into the handful the test singles out, ending as a 20-dot quantile dotplot with 4 filled
exclusions: no Bayes algebra, no uncertainty-technique roster, no HOPs/fan charts; keep Gigerenzer numbers approximate as the chapter itself does
